# Go Agent migration baseline

`go-agent-spool.json` is an auditable row-level snapshot generated by the real Go
Agent at commit `1d892c9e00005d497cfbc8660a5dd67b22d4da29`, before removal of the
Go platform implementation. It contains the original SQLite `CREATE TABLE`
statements, typed integers, base64 BLOBs, identity and original incoming batches.
All identities, keys and telemetry in this fixture are synthetic.

Generation used `internal/agent.New` and `Accept` for two OTLP JSON batches,
`OpenQueue.Retry` twice for the first, and `OpenQueue.Complete` for the second.
A synthetic exact-int64 log cursor and binary prefix were added through SQLite.
The test freezes its clock at `generated_at`, restores the schema and rows, then
verifies Node reads and replays the pending batch without changing its bytes or
retry metadata, keeps the completed receipt, and persists the same identity.
The fixture avoids requiring the deleted Go implementation or toolchain.

Before this static fixture was created, the migration suite additionally passed
a live Go → Node → Go round-trip: Go accepted a batch, Node reopened the original
spool, replayed/deduplicated/completed it, and Go reopened the Node-written spool
and confirmed the same identity and zero queued batches. Together with the OTLP
Go differential cases, the Agent/OTLP suite passed 21 tests with no skips.

`go-center-compat.json` records Go `encoding/json` output for trace events/links,
`strconv.FormatFloat` decimal results, and SHA256 SDK configuration revisions
using the public Go SDK structs and `UseNumber`. It covers exact int64/numeric
lexemes, default fields, map ordering, HTML escaping, null/empty collections and
rounding ties. These expected values were generated with Go, not by the Node
implementation under test.

## Historical privileged Agent unit

`legacy-privileged-agent.service` preserves the exact unit shipped at commit
`fd3685e5011c7762ef491cd8fca0ec493b8c555e`. It is an inert regression fixture,
never installed into the host systemd. Isolated installer/maintenance tests use
it to prove that Docker supplementary groups, capabilities and the former web
write path cannot return through automatic restoration or retained rollback.
